newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan pork buying seen slack after July surge.
newsitem.headline: Japan pork buying seen slack after July surge.

text.p: Japan's pork buying is likely to be slow in the near term, after shipments from abroad and from bonded warehouses in Japan rose massively during July, local traders said on Monday.
Traders estimated Japan's pork imports were around 100,000 tonnes in July, up sharply from 17,982 tonnes in June.

Japan's pork imports in the January-June period of this year totalled 171,310 tonnes, against 438,967 tonnes a year earlier, Finance Ministry data shows. The ministry is to announce import figures for July later this month.

"We were waiting for the lifting of an emergency import tariff from July 1. It's natural that everybody rushed to bring pork here to take advantage of a lower tariff," a pork trader at a major trade house said.
The emergency import tariff had been put in place to limit an influx of foreign pork.

The Agriculture and Livestock Industries Corp, an industry promotion body, said that Japan's pork stocks totalled 87,609 tonnes at end-June, while bonded warehouses across the country held 60,416 tonnes of pork.
Traders said pork shipments from the bonded warehouses were partly behind the import surge.
Another pork trader at a major trade house in Tokyo said: "Japan's pork buying from abroad will be slow in the near term, after the huge quantity imported in July."
U.S. pork traders have been looking for Japan to start buying large amounts of U.S. pork since Tokyo banned pork exported by Taiwan due to an outbreak there of foot and mouth disease.
But some trade house officials in Tokyo said offer prices for U.S. pork were too high for them to buy.

"It's naive to expect a lack of Taiwanese pork to lead to buying of U.S. pork automatically. European pork is quite competitive at the moment," a senior official of another trade house's livestock department said.
